assumptions: Rule-based scoring
Seed graph only
No external data
falsification_criteria: Composite mean below 0.3 after 50 benchmarks indicates fundamental pipeline failure.

name: Airships
citation: evidence/failures/airships.json `resurrection_conditions` lists 'Lockheed LMH-1, LTA Research' as active resurrection projects. Public record: LTA Research Pathfinder 1 first flight 2024; HAV Airlander 10 first flight 2016.

name: Iridium
citation: evidence/failures/iridium.json documents the original failure. Public record: Iridium Communications (IRDM) relaunched and operates a 66-satellite LEO constellation for IoT/voice as of 2026.

name: Segway
citation: evidence/failures/segway.json: production ended 2020. No successor product for the personal-balancing-transport category exists. Micro-mobility shifted to shared e-scooters (Bird, Lime), which are a different product class.

name: Concorde
citation: evidence/failures/concorde.json. Public record: Boom Supersonic XB-1 supersonic flight Oct 2024; Overture not in commercial service as of 2026. Partial: tech demonstrator exists, no commercial resurrection yet.

name: Google Glass
citation: evidence/failures/google_glass.json. Enterprise Edition discontinued 2023. No like-for-like successor; AR headsets are a different product class.

name: Theranos
citation: evidence/failures/theranos.json. Founder convicted of fraud 2022. The underlying scientific claim was false, not premature — no resurrection is possible without invalidating the original premise.

name: Quibi
citation: evidence/failures/quibi.json. Shut down 2020. The category of premium short-form mobile video was obsoleted by TikTok, not resurrected by a successor.

name: Betamax
citation: evidence/failures/betamax.json. Production ended 2016. VHS-then-streaming successorship obsoleted the format; no resurrection.

name: HD-DVD
citation: evidence/failures/hd_dvd.json. Discontinued 2008. Blu-ray won the format war; streaming obsoleted physical media. No resurrection.

claim: Commercially available selective emitter materials with measured emissivity >0.9 in the 8-13 µm atmospheric transparency window will exist by 2027-06-01, making APRM missing_prerequisite selective_emitters resolvable.
evidence: APRM candidate lists selective_emitters as missing_prerequisite
Radiative cooling research has accelerated since 2014 (Fan group, Stanford)
Multiple papers report >0.9 emissivity in lab (e.g., Zhai et al. Science 2017)
Commercial startups exist: SkyCool Systems, Radi-Cool
The 8-13 µm window is well-characterized and stable
counterevidence: Lab materials may not be commercially scalable by 2027
Cost per m2 may be too high for APRM target market (off-grid preservation)
Durability under outdoor conditions is largely untested
No standardized commercial spec for radiative cooling materials exists yet
assumptions: Commercial availability means purchasable by a research lab, not mass-market
Emissivity >0.9 is measured in the 8-13 µm band specifically
Resolution date 2027-06-01 allows ~10 months from now for market development
falsification_criteria: If no commercial supplier offers a material with measured emissivity >0.9 in 8-13 µm by 2027-06-01, the prediction fails. If one or more suppliers exist, it passes.
